newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses rise steeply on U.S. trade data.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses rise steeply on U.S. trade data.

text.p: European bourses picked up strongly on Thursday as a drop in the U.S. trade deficit gave Wall Street a head start, the third day running New York has forged ahead.
On currency markets, the better-than-expected U.S. trade figures also boosted the dollar which climbed half a pfennig against the mark and strengthened against the yen.

Europe's optimistic mood was underpinned by the buoyancy in New York. Bourses on both sides of the Atlantic rose in pre-Christmas holiday business on Wednesday and the pattern was much the same on Thursday.

The Dow Jones industrial powered ahead 0.75 percent in early trade after figures showed the U.S. trade gap narrowed sharply in October as overseas sales of aircraft surged. New York put on 38 points to 6,346 on Wednesday in an end-of-year rush to snap up technology stocks.

London climbed 0.7 percent with trading also enlivened by a pre-Christmas bidding spree with companies going shopping for takeover targets, putting a price tag of more than two billion pounds ($3.3 billion) on their list of potential purchases.
Firms have launched five major bids for British companies this week -- most of them hostile -- injecting life into the normally dull holiday period for dealmakers.

Corporate financiers say the unusual end-of-the-year dash may be due to a perceived need to finish deals ahead of a possible change in government next year and a desire to take advantage of high stock prices.

"Markets tend to be reasonably buoyant in the new year, and so therefore, if you're relying on an equity funding, it's probably not a bad time," said Robert Swannell, head of UK corporate finance at Schroders.
Paris was the best performer, climbing sharply by 1.34 percent. Market spirits were lifted by New York and a flurry of merger-related announcements in the pharmaceuticals and retail sectors.
Elf Aquitaine and Sanofi rose strongly after Elf said it would be desirable for its pharmaceutical unit Sanofi to merge with other laboratories to boost profitability.
Rhone-Poulenc climbed 0.6 percent to 167 francs. The drugs group is merging its animal health business with Merck to create a venture with 8.5 billion francs ($1.6 billion) in annual sales.

In Frankfurt, stocks on the computerised IBIS index jumped on the U.S. trade figures to register a gain of 0.5 percent at mid-afternoon. Floor trading, which ended before the U.S. data was issued, finished down 0.46 percent.

On the currency front, the dollar strengthened against the mark after the trade figures and climbed on the yen after Tokyo shares tumbled overnight to their low of the year amid deepening gloom about Japan's economic outlook.
"The much better-than-expected headline number clearly boosted the dollar," said Nick Stamenkovic at DKB International.

But the details of the trade report showed the politically sensitive trade gap with Japan surging again. The gap rose 30.9 percent to $4.96 billion, the highest since August 1995 because of increased car and car parts imports.
Some U.S. manufacturers charge Japan is deliberately manipulating its currency to keep the yen's value low and make its products cheaper for American importers.
The U.S. currency climbed to 1.5601 marks well above the level of 1.5541 in late trade on Wednesday amid some uncertainty over the direction of German interest rates.

The Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged at its meeting but some traders said an outside chance remained that the bank would fix its key securities repurchase rate slightly lower over the year-end holiday period.
The Swiss franc was lower in Europe, meantime, and set a two-year low at 1.3372 per dollar and a three-year low at 85.82 centimes per mark at one point.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5601 marks and 114.03 yen, compared with 1.5541 and 113.65 in late business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1545 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 27.1 points at 4,045.3.
In Frankfurt, the 30-share DAX ended 13.00 lower at 2,807.75 points. The after-hours IBIS index was up 12.92 points at 2827.15.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 30.30 at 2,249.19.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $369.00 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $369.10. Silver was at $4.88, up two cents.
